links.comparator_used: AI alone generating the adapted physical activity protocol without professional involvement (novice professional with AI support vs AI alone; expert-only protocols also rated)
links.outcome: Blinded panel-rated overall quality of adapted physical activity protocols (effectiveness, safety, appropriateness, clarity, progression) across five orthopedic conditions
links.effect: NAI protocols were rated significantly higher than AI-alone protocols in most conditions (p < 0.01), except osteoporosis (p = 0.362). Expert-only protocols scored highest, then NAI, then AI alone (all p < 0.05). EP vs AI differences were largest for safety (p < 0.01), appropriateness/tailoring (p < 0.01) and progression (p < 0.05).
links.tradeoff: NAI protocols still scored below expert-only protocols, so the expertise gap was only partly closed. AI-alone protocols varied more across pathologies. No benefit of NAI over AI alone was seen for osteoporosis.
links.quote: AI-generated protocols without human oversight are not yet suitable for autonomous APA prescription, supporting a complementary, expertise-dependent role of AI in exercise programming.

design_hint: human professional oversight of AI-generated exercise prescriptions
